title: Trading is a minus-sum game due to commissions and slippage
claim: After accounting for commissions and slippage, trading transaction costs make it a minus-sum game where total payoffs are less than total costs.
support: Study guide answer states: When winner receives less than loser lost, transaction is minus-sum game
mechanism: Each trade incurs entry and exit commissions plus slippage on both sides
assumptions: Broker commissions apply to both sides
validation: Quantifiable: Compare gross P&L to net P&L after costs

title: Three pillars of successful trading
claim: Successful trading requires three pillars: sound psychology, good analytic method, and careful money management
support: Study guide explicitly lists these three elements as non-negotiable
mechanism: Psychology prevents emotional errors; method generates signals; money management sizes exposure
assumptions: Deficiency in one cannot be compensated by others

title: Commissions and slippage as primary drag on small accounts
claim: Fixed commissions as percentage of capital create disproportionate drag on accounts under 100k; margin amplifies this effect
support: Worked example: 100 shares at 20 with 10 commission = 1% round-trip cost; on 50% margin becomes 2% of capital
mechanism: Small trade size means commissions are larger percentage of notional; margin reduces capital base, increasing percentage impact

title: Professional trader measures risk
claim: Successful traders measure each risk in advance and trade only when odds are clearly favorable
support: Study guide distinguishes professional risk measurement from amateur emotional reactions
mechanism: Measurement and pre-decision prevents emotional override during execution

title: Personal discipline in trading mirrors discipline in life
claim: Traders replicate their life patterns in the market; personal irresponsibility predicts trading losses
support: Worked example: trader with traffic tickets, tax penalties, and trading losses advised to work on personal discipline
mechanism: Lack of discipline manifests consistently across all domains
failure_modes: Treating trading as separate domain from life

title: Stopping trading after losses improves recovery
claim: After losing streak, stopping to analyze causes prevents compulsive revenge trading and improves outcomes
support: Study guide recommends analysis pause after 20% drawdown; gambling behavior includes inability to stop
mechanism: Reflection period allows recalibration; prevents irrational retaliation trades

title: Commercial systems fail due to curve-fitting
claim: Purchased trading systems are optimized on historical data and break when markets change; curve-fitting is lethal
support: Study guide: Systems built on old data self-destruct when markets change
mechanism: Curve-fitting to historical patterns; market regime shifts invalidate historical patterns

title: Gambling attitude signals in trading
claim: Gambling attitude signals include: inability to resist urge to trade, emotional swings (elation/shame), reversing losing positions
support: Study guide lists multiple behavioral indicators of gambling mindset
mechanism: Emotional decision-making replaces rational risk management

title: Position size should not increase after wins
claim: After successful trades, position sizing should remain constant (risk same percentage), not increase in size
support: Study guide: Only increase if percentage risk stays same; warns against becoming sloppy after lucky streak
mechanism: Fixed risk percentage ensures consistent drawdown bounds; increasing size increases maximum drawdown exposure

title: Accept personal responsibility is recovery first step
claim: Trader must acknowledge personal responsibility for losses; searching for systems without self-examination leads nowhere
support: Study guide: Accepting responsibility clears illusions and puts trading on realistic footing
mechanism: Ownership enables pattern recognition; blame externalization prevents learning

title: Discipline and plans outweigh capital or connections
claim: Written trade plans implemented with discipline are most critical to success, more than capital size or social connections
support: Study guide ranks discipline above capital size, social connections, and prior success
mechanism: Pre-written plans prevent emotional override; discipline ensures execution

title: Trader impulsivity causes perceived market chaos
claim: Trader impulsivity creates perception of confusing markets more than information shortage or capital constraints
support: Study guide identifies trader impulsivity as primary source of perceived market chaos
mechanism: Emotional decision-making prevents coherent pattern recognition

title: Systems fail when parameters optimized on history
claim: Systems optimized to fit historical data fail out-of-sample; walk-forward testing detects curve-fitting
support: Study guide emphasizes systems designed to fit old data self-destruct when markets change
mechanism: Curve-fitting captures noise and regime-specific patterns, not generalizable signal

title: Position sizing discipline is non-negotiable
claim: Proper risk management prioritizes position size control; many traders devise good strategies but fail in execution
support: Study guide emphasizes position sizing as non-negotiable risk management element
mechanism: Fixed fraction or Kelly Criterion sizing limits maximum drawdown

title: Fixed risk percentage bounds drawdown
claim: If each trade risks fixed percentage of equity, maximum drawdown is predictable and bounded
support: Study guide discusses position sizing frameworks for risk control
mechanism: Mathematical: max loss = consecutive losses × risk percentage

title: Limit orders reduce entry slippage
claim: Use limit orders for entries to reduce slippage; tradeoff is possibility of missing entry
support: Study guide example shows $8 slippage on market order; limit orders eliminate upside slippage
mechanism: Limit orders execute at specified price or not; market orders accept best available

title: Market-if-touched orders for stops
claim: For stop losses, use market-if-touched orders rather than limit orders to ensure execution
support: Study guide recommends MIT to ensure exit; limit orders may fail to execute during gaps
mechanism: MIT becomes market order when triggered, guaranteeing execution even if slippage occurs

title: Trade diary critical for feedback loop
claim: Maintaining detailed trade records enables pattern recognition and continuous improvement
support: Study guide dedicates chapter to record-keeping; emphasizes as essential feedback mechanism
mechanism: Recorded data reveals patterns invisible in real-time; enables statistical analysis
